title: Remove synchronized network anchors; decouple subnet lifecycle and upgrade AWS provider safely
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We have recurring plan churn and occasional failures when applying Terraform changes to VPC subnets and NAT gateways due to a synchronized 'network anchor' pattern used across multiple workspaces. This ticket removes the synchronized anchor resource, decouples ephemeral vs persistent networking state, and performs a controlled upgrade to the AWS provider v5.x to benefit from SDK stability and new lifecycle behaviors. Goals: 1) eliminate anchor-induced lock contention during parallel deploys, 2) make subnet lifecycle idempotent across workspaces, 3) complete provider upgrade without downtime, and 4) document migration steps and rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: All overlay workspaces can run terraform plan/apply concurrently without anchor lock regression
Subnet resources are managed by a single owner module with clear split between ephemeral and persistent state
Automated CI runs provider v5.x against the staging environment with no plan drift for 7 days
Runbook and rollback steps published in Confluence and reviewed by SRE
No customer-facing incidents attributable to this change during canary rollout
risks: Provider upgrade may change default behaviors for certain resource attributes (eg. tag propagation) leading to unexpected diffs
State migration between modules risks accidental re-creation if addressability changes
Concurrent applies without a safe coordination mechanism could temporarily affect route table associations
decisions: Do a blue/green provider upgrade strategy: stage -> canary -> full, rather than a single global bump
Introduce a lightweight migration shim (TF import + idempotent resource verification) rather than a wholesale resource move
Keep the legacy anchor code in a gated branch until verification completes and then remove in two-step PRs to make rollbacks trivial
work_items: Create a single authoritative networking module that owns persistent subnet IDs and exposes ephemeral overlay inputs
Add a resource-level 'managed_by' tag to assert ownership during CI validations
Implement a terraform plan validator in CI to fail on unexpected destroy/create of persistent resources
Write an import script (golang) used by the migration job to reconcile state without re-creating resources
Upgrade aws provider in a dedicated branch and run full TF plan/apply in staging under monitoring
Schedule a weekend canary for a low-risk region and monitor infra-health dashboards for 12 hours before rolling out

rollout_plan: Phase 1: Staging validation - run import shim and provider v5.x in staging for 72 hours
Phase 2: Canary in low-traffic region (us-west-2) with 2-hour observation windows and alerts on route/nat anomalies
Phase 3: Gradual expansion to remaining regions over 3 days with monitor gating
Phase 4: Merge removal of legacy anchor after successful full rollout
